hook: Hyderabad-made dome maps babies' side vision: *10 of 20* showed loss
hook_b: Hyderabad-made dome maps babies' side vision: *10 of 20* showed loss
tldr: Researchers at L V Prasad Eye Institute tested the Baby Vision Screener (BaViS), which tracks babies' eye movements to LED lights to detect early vision loss from primary congenital glaucoma.

beats.what: A baby lies under a dome; LEDs flash from the edge towards the centre along 12 directions while an examiner tracks eye shifts via infrared camera.
beats.why: In primary congenital glaucoma side vision is damaged, and infants can't speak or follow instructions, making early loss hard to measure.
beats.care: The study, in the Journal of Glaucoma, suggests doctors may spot and track vision loss in babies years earlier.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Of 29 young patients tested, reliable maps came for 20; half of them showed narrowing of the visual field.

facts.t: LEDs flash along *12* directions from the dome's edge to its centre.

viz.l: Mapped children with narrowed side vision
viz.verdict: Half the mapped children already had measurable vision loss.

learn.t: Primary congenital glaucoma = high eye pressure present from birth that damages the optic nerve and can cause permanent blindness.

watch: Whether BaViS moves from study to wider clinical use.

fact: LVPEI's LED dome mapped side vision in babies as young as *2.3 months*
twist: There are no commercial automated side-vision machines for infants; doctors usually wave a toy to test.
